notes: Parts are the same as step 1 except that both boards now use a new type, arduino-mkr-wan-1300-pins. The catalogue card for arduino-mkr-wan-1300 has only power ports (GND, VCC, 5V, VIN, USB, BATT) and no digital pins, but both circuits wire digital pin 2, which the card cannot express. The new type keeps those ports and adds the pin header, with pin 2 as D2 (the same naming as the other MKR cards).

The pushbutton now sits across the centre gap, as its card requires. Top half (image top block, bank 'b'): 1.l in column 5 and 2.l in column 7. Bottom half (bank 't'): 1.r in column 5 and 2.r in column 7. Columns 5 and 7 are the columns the image uses for its legs, and the black GND wire and the yellow pin 2 wire stay on those columns. Because 1.l/1.r are joined inside and 2.l/2.r are joined inside, GND (column 5) and D2 (column 7) are on opposite sides of the switch, so pressing the button pulls D2 low (INPUT_PULLUP). The image draws the button on one half only; the card's rule for this part takes priority here.

The breadboard images label the top block rows j-f and the bottom block e-a, which is the reverse of the catalogue's naming. The image's top block is therefore written as bank 'b' (rows f-j), and the bottom block as bank 't' (rows a-e). Row f is next to the centre gap.
On the sender, the jumper wires are in row g and the button legs in row f. They are in the same column strips as in the image, so the connections are the same.

Receiver: the LED cathode (straight leg) is in column 6, which the black wire takes to GND. The LED anode (bent, longer leg) is in column 8 and goes to the resistor in 8-11 of row g. The green wire from D2 is in column 11. So the resistor is on the anode side.
The resistor value is not given in the manual, so 220 ohm is assumed.
Each antenna connects to its board through its own cable. The board type has no antenna port, so that edge has no port on the board side.
The micro USB cables are not drawn in the images. Each is joined to its board's USB port, since the parts list requires them.
The two circuits are separate builds, with no electrical link between them. LoRa radio is the only link.
